title: Made my first incremental game with the help of AI. What do you guys think?
author: m7mdq89
selftext:
Hey everyone!

I’m a big fan of incremental games, so I decided to make one myself!

It’s called One More Nugget, a mining incremental game where you collect gold and unlock upgrades.

I’ve been using AI tools throughout development, including Codex for coding and AI for some of the assets.

It’s my first game, and I just released the trailer and Steam page!

What do you guys think? Would love to hear your feedback!

Steam (Wishlist):

https://store.steampowered.com/app/5535070/One\_More\_Nugget/

Trailer:

https://youtu.be/LKs2FO7VCvs

comments.author: aigamedev-mod
comments.body:
Hey u/m7mdq89, this falls under Rule 4. Sharing your game is okay here, free or paid, but you need to talk about how it was developed using AI, so the community has something to discuss. This post doesn't have enough on that yet.

To keep it up, edit your post or reply to this comment within an hour with some details on your dev process, like:

- which AI tools you used, and what for
- how they fit into your workflow
- problems you hit and how you dealt with them

"Made with AI", a list of tools or a ChatGPT bullet list won't cut it. If nothing's added by then, this post may be removed.

If you think we got this wrong, [message the mods](https://www.reddit.com/message/compose?to=/r/aigamedev).

replies.author: m7mdq89
replies.body:
Hey, thanks for the heads up

I’ve been developing One More Nugget in Unity, using Codex to help with programming and AI for some of the visual assets.

My workflow is basically coming up with the gameplay mechanics and upgrades myself, then working with Codex to implement them. I test everything in Unity, see what feels right, and keep making changes until I’m happy with it.

One of the biggest challenges has actually been keeping the art consistent. AI-generated assets don’t always match the style I’m going for, so I’ve had to redo and adjust quite a few things to make everything fit together.

It’s been a lot of trial and error, especially getting the gameplay and progression to feel satisfying.

Hope that gives a better idea of how I’ve been working on it
